subject: Acme Corp — Performance / SLO follow-up and proposed SLA language
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Miller <john.miller@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Acme follow-up — performance targets & next steps

Hi John,

Great to speak with you this morning — thanks for the demo and for walking through Acme's primary read/write/search flows. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the performance targets and proposed next steps so we can align engineering + procurement.

Quick recap of the targets you called out:
- Latency targets: p50 <= 60ms; p95 <= 250ms for single-turn text generation (50 token responses)
- Throughput: steady-state 300 requests/minute across the tenant
- Concurrency: expected burst concurrency up to 150 concurrent requests (peak 30 minutes/day)
- Streaming: client needs low-latency streaming for partial tokens for chat UI (chunked responses acceptable)

Open questions we flagged:
1) How are you planning to measure latency — from client SDK send time, arrival at edge, or token issuance?
2) For streaming, do you need strict per-token latency SLOs or an end-to-end time-to-first-byte requirement?
3) Any exclusions you want in the SLA for planned maintenance, DDoS, or customer-originated throttling?

Next steps I propose:
- I'll share a short draft SLA clause capturing measurement definitions and proposed reporting cadence (weekly for <90 days, then monthly). Attached is a perf worksheet you can populate with traffic profiles (acme_perf_requirements.xlsx).
- Aditya will validate feasibility against our Dedicated capacity configs and confirm queuing/KV cache impacts.
- If this looks good, we can provide a redlineable SLA PDF for procurement.

I've attached a one-page performance worksheet and a starting SLA draft for your team to review.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: John Miller <john.miller@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme follow-up — performance targets & next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Latency measurement: we measure from when our front-end service emits the request to when the first token is returned to the client (time-to-first-byte for streaming; for non-streaming the first token). If you need, we can switch to a synthetic agent that measures from edge to token.
- Streaming SLO: we care most about time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and then max inter-token gap. If you can commit to p95 TTFB <= 300ms for streaming requests that'd be great.
- Exclusions: planned maintenance windows are fine (we'd expect 72h notice for major upgrades). DDoS will be managed by us with a shared mitigation plan — we can discuss carve-outs.

Procurement asked for proposed reporting cadence and remedies (credits). Can you outline how you measure p95 (server-side logs vs client measurements), how often you push reports, and what remedies you typically offer for SLA breaches?

John
Director of Product Engineering | Acme Corp
john.miller@acme.com | +1 (617) 555-9987
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: John Miller <john.miller@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme follow-up — performance targets & next steps

Thanks John — helpful. Below is a proposed SLA language snippet that we can circulate to procurement as a starting point. Aditya / Neha / David — please add technical comments inline if anything looks infeasible.

PROPOSED SLA SNIPPET (draft):
- Measurement: Latency SLOs (p50/p95) are measured server-side at the Redwood edge closest to the request origin using our production telemetry. For streaming requests, Time-to-First-Byte (TTFB) is the metric for initial response; inter-token gaps are monitored but not currently covered by financial remedies.
- Exclusions: SLA does not apply to (a) scheduled maintenance with 72 hours' notice, (b) force majeure events (including DDoS beyond reasonable mitigation), (c) customer misconfiguration or abuse, (d) third-party network outages beyond Redwood's control.
- Reporting cadence: Weekly rolling reports for the first 90 days post-onboarding, then monthly reports thereafter. Detailed latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95) will be included along with aggregated throughput and error rates.
- Remedies: For any calendar month where p95 latency exceeds the committed target by more than 10%, customer is eligible for a service credit equal to 10% of that month's usage charges for the impacted route. Severe sustained breaches (p95 > 2x target for >72 contiguous hours) will trigger an executive review and potential bespoke remedies.

Open items for engineering:
- Confirm that our server-side measurement (edge-to-first-token) aligns with Acme's client-side instrumentation. If not, we should agree to a joint tagging strategy or synthetic agents.
- Confirm whether we can include per-token inter-gap monitoring as a non-financial SLA (operational alerting only).

If that language is OK, I'll convert it into a redlineable PDF for Procurement.

Best,
Marissa

Attachment: acme_sla_draft.pdf (updated draft)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Acme follow-up — performance targets & next steps

Looping in a quick engineering assessment — internal only.

Short answers:
- Measurement: We can measure p50/p95 at the edge (time from request receipt at edge to first token emitted). That is what our production telemetry reports today. Client-side instrumentation typically adds network variance; if Acme wants parity we should run a short instrumented test with a synthetic client in their region.
- Throughput/Concurrency: 300 req/min steady-state with bursts to 150 concurrent is feasible on a single Dedicated pool (N1 units) with a burst config. We'll call out suggested buffer headroom: provision for 20% overhead to avoid queueing spikes.
- Streaming: We can guarantee p95 TTFB <= 300ms for single-turn streaming under normal conditions on Dedicated with the recommended headroom. Inter-token gaps are more workload-dependent (model size, sampling). We can provide operational monitoring for gaps but not include financial remedies initially.
- Reporting: We can generate weekly rolling CSVs from our telemetry pipeline and provide a monthly SLA report.

Suggested edits to SLA snippet:
- Change remedy: 10% credit is fine as a starting proposal but cap at 50% of that month's route charges.
- Add definition: "normal conditions" excludes customer-originated traffic spikes that exceed declared traffic profile by >3x.

I'll prep a short tech note to append to the SLA draft (latency measurement definition, example logs, and proposed synthetic test).

- Aditya
Principal SRE | Redwood Inference
